value.body: A pre-primary teacher works with children aged about three to six in nursery, LKG and UKG classes. Private pre-schools, play schools and the pre-primary sections of schools hire them. A day involves circle time, play-based activities, early reading and number work, snacks and rest routines, and talking to parents at pick-up.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: An early childhood (ECCE / nursery teacher) diploma or D.El.Ed
items.note: Requirements differ from school to school

items.label: Where the work is
items.value: Private pre-schools, play schools and school pre-primary sections

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Schools and play schools hire directly, often asking for an early childhood or nursery teacher training diploma, a D.El.Ed or a degree, along with spoken English and a short demo class. Government pre-primary teaching posts are few and follow state rules.

value.title: At a glance
items: Pay at small play schools is often modest and varies widely.
NEP 2020 treats ages 3–8 as one foundational stage, which is adding pre-primary sections to schools.
Next roles: primary teacher, coordinator, or running a play school.
